activity: to turn on a tablet, open a drawing app and put it away when done
knowledge_domain: to turn on a tablet, open a drawing app and put it away when done
story:
Ibrahim went to his friend Nadia's house. She had a tablet on the table. Ibrahim wanted to draw a cat on it. "It sleeps," said Nadia. "Watch this."

Nadia pushed the little round button. The screen woke up. It went from black to bright. Ibrahim clapped. "Again, again!" he said. Nadia let him push the button. Tap. The screen was black. Tap. The screen was bright. "I can do it too!" said Ibrahim.

Then Nadia showed him a blue square. "Tap this one," she said. Ibrahim tapped it. The drawing app opened. There was a green shape on the screen. Ibrahim drew a cat with one ear and five legs. Nadia laughed. "That is a silly cat," she said. "He is sorry about his legs," said Ibrahim.

When they finished, Nadia put the tablet in a basket. "It sleeps there," she said. Ibrahim tapped the button first. The screen went dark. Then he laid the tablet down, soft as a sleeping cat.

activity: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
knowledge_domain: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
story:
Jayden wanted to give his mama a present. He looked in his toy box. He found a small blue car. It was just right.

Jayden carried the car to the kitchen. Mama was there. Steam rose up from a big pot. Jayden reached out his hand. "Not the pot, love," Mama said. She picked him up. "The pot is hot. It can hurt you."

Jayden looked at the pot from Mama's arms. A little ice cube sat on the counter. It was melting. It got smaller and smaller. Then it was just a wet spot. "Ice is cold," said Jayden. "Hot pot, cold ice." Mama smiled. "Yes, my smart boy."

Jayden slid down and held Mama's leg with one hand. He kept the car safe in the other hand. He stayed right there, close to Mama. The pot went bubble, bubble. Jayden did not touch it. He watched the steam go up.

When the cooking was done, Jayden held out the car. "Present for you, Mama!" Mama knelt down and took it. "Thank you, Jayden." She gave him a big, warm hug.

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
story:
Joshua went to Mia's house. Mia had a big toy kitchen. Joshua wanted to make soup like a grown-up.

Mia gave him a pot and a spoon. Joshua put in a red block. He put in a blue cup. He began to stir. Round and round went the spoon. "Look, my soup is moving!" he said.

Then Baby Bear fell on the floor. Baby Bear began to cry. Well, Mia made him cry. "Oh no," said Mia. "Baby Bear is hungry." Joshua held out his pot. Would soup help a bear? He tipped the spoon near Baby Bear's mouth. Mia made slurping sounds. Then she stopped crying the bear. "He feels better," she said. The soup had made the crying stop. Joshua's eyes got big.

After that, Baby Bear got tired. Joshua wrapped him in a small towel. He patted the bear's back, softly, softly. Soon the bear went to sleep.

At home time, Mia gave Joshua the spoon to keep. He held it all the way to the car. "More soup tomorrow," he said.

activity: to turn on a tablet, open a drawing app and put it away when done
knowledge_domain: to turn on a tablet, open a drawing app and put it away when done
story:
Charlotte went to her friend Mia's house. Mia had a tablet. Charlotte wanted to draw on it. "Can I try?" she asked.

Mia's mom said, "Yes. First you press the little button." Charlotte pressed it. The screen lit up. She pressed it again. The screen went dark. "Oops," said Charlotte. She pressed it one more time. The screen came back. Charlotte laughed.

Mia showed her the drawing app. Charlotte tapped it. Colors filled the screen. She drew a big green hill. She drew a yellow sun on top. She drew a red bird. Then she was done. "Now we put it away," said Mia's mom. Charlotte pressed the button. The screen went dark. She laid the tablet on the table. "I did it all by myself," said Charlotte. "Same time tomorrow?" asked Mia. "Yes," said Charlotte. "I want to draw a cat."

activity: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
knowledge_domain: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
story:
Sarah ran into the library. She held Mama's hand tight. "Books!" said Sarah. "So many books!"

A big rug sat in the corner. Sarah saw bins on the rug. Each bin had toys in it. One bin had little animals. One bin had trucks and balls. One bin had play food. Sarah wanted them all.

She picked up a little cat. She put it in the animal bin. Then she found a banana. It did not look right next to the cat. She moved the banana to the food bin. The banana sat with the apples and the bread. Sarah clapped. "Mama, look! Bananas go with food!"

A boy dropped his teddy bear. It fell near the food bin. Sarah picked it up. The bear was soft, not rough like the carpet. "Bear goes with toys," said Sarah. She put it in the toy bin. The boy smiled.

Then Sarah found a picture book. She opened it. There was a dog in the picture. There was a cake, too. "Dog is an animal. Cake is food," said Sarah. Mama laughed. Sarah turned the page, quick and excited.

activity: to hold a pencil correctly and write the letters of their own first name
knowledge_domain: to hold a pencil correctly and write the letters of their own first name
story:
Max sat at the kitchen table. His mom put a pencil in his hand. "Let's write your name," she said.

Max squeezed the pencil in his fist. He pushed it down hard. The tip snapped off. The little piece rolled across the table and dropped to the floor.

"Oops," said Max. His big brother Tom came to look. Tom picked up the broken tip. He showed Max his own hand. Tom held the pencil light, like a little bird sitting on his fingers.

Max tried it. He held the pencil the same way. He did not push hard. Now the pencil made a line. The line did not break. He made a big M. Then an A. Then an X.

The letters sat on the paper, side by side. "That's my name!" said Max. He looked at the pencil. Was it magic? No, it was just his hand, holding soft and slow. He wrote his name again.

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
story:
Nicholas was at Grandma's house. He found a big cardboard box under the table. He peeked inside. There was a blanket, a small cup, and a teddy bear. "Whose box is this?" he asked. Grandma smiled. "It was Mommy's box. She played house with it."

Nicholas wanted to play too. He set the teddy bear on the blanket. He held the cup to the bear's mouth. The bear tipped over and fell. The bear looked grumpy lying there. "Are you hungry?" Nicholas asked. "Yes," he said in a bear voice. He pretended to feed the bear a pretend snack. The bear sat up tall.

Then Nicholas wrapped the bear in the blanket. He rocked the bear side to side. He counted, "One, two, three," softly. The bear's eyes began to close. Nicholas patted the bear's back. "Shh," he whispered. Grandma peeked in and smiled. "Goodnight, baby bear," said Nicholas.

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
story:
Willow ran to the play corner at school. She wanted to play house with her bear. But Ben had the toy stove, and Mia had the little bed. Willow's bear had nowhere to sleep and nothing to cook. She sat down on her knee and thought.

Then she had an idea. She took an empty box and tipped it over. Now the bear had a bed! She patted the box and laid the bear down. "Sleep tight, baby bear," she said. The bear closed his eyes, as if he could not stay awake. Ben saw the box and clapped. "A bed from a box!" he said. Mia put her pot on the box's edge. "Now we can cook soup next to the bear."

The teacher came to look. "What a fine house," she said. "Can I visit?" Willow nodded fast. "Wipe your feet first," she said. The teacher wiped her shoes on the mat, very slowly. Then she sat on a tiny chair, and it looked too small for her. Everybody laughed. "More soup, please," said the teacher, holding out her cup.

activity: to share a toy with a classmate and wait for a turn without grabbing
knowledge_domain: to share a toy with a classmate and wait for a turn without grabbing
story:
Gianna was at Milo's birthday party. A big red truck sat on the grass. It had a shovel that could dig deep holes. Gianna wanted it so much.

Ben grabbed the truck first. "My turn," he said. Gianna reached out her hand. Then she stopped. She put her hands in her lap instead. Ben dug a thin little hole in the dirt. Seeds went in the hole for a party game. Then Ben held out the truck. "Your turn now," he said.

Gianna took the truck. She dug a big hole. It was deep and round. "Look, Ben!" she said. Ben clapped his hands. "Now my turn again?" he asked. "Yes," said Gianna. "Then my turn." The truck went back and forth, back and forth. "Best diggers ever," said Ben.

activity: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
knowledge_domain: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
story:
Olivia went to the garden center with Dad. The sun felt warm on her nose. The store was loud with carts and voices. Olivia wanted to grow her own carrots.

She picked a small bag of seeds. Dad got a big pot and soft brown dirt. At home, they sat on the step. Olivia patted the dirt down flat. Then she dropped three tiny seeds on top. She covered them with a little more dirt. Dad poured water from a small cup.

Every morning Olivia ran outside. She saw nothing. She saw dirt. She pouted. "Where are my carrots?" she asked. Dad said, "Look again tomorrow."

The weather turned hot. The sun burned Olivia's bare toes on the step, so Dad got her little sandals. After that, the pot showed something green. One small leaf, then two. Olivia gasped and touched it gently.

The leaves grew tall and feathery. Dad held the pot steady. Together they pulled up one fat orange carrot. It was cold and crunchy and smelled like dirt and rain. Olivia washed it under the tap and took a big bite.

"My seed made this," said Olivia. Dad smiled. "Let's plant some more tomorrow."

activity: to say a family blessing or greeting before a shared meal
knowledge_domain: to say a family blessing or greeting before a shared meal
story:
Ivy went to the cemetery with Mama and Pop. They carried a picnic basket. They were going to eat lunch near Grandpa Ben's stone. The stone felt dry and warm in the sun.

Mama set out the food on a red blanket. There were bread, cheese, and sweet grapes. Ivy wanted to grab a grape right away. "First we say our greeting," said Pop. He held out his hand. Ivy did not know the words yet.

Pop held Mama's hand. Mama held Ivy's hand. Then they all held hands in a circle. "One, two, three," said Pop. They said the greeting together. Ivy said the words too. Then Pop smiled. Then Mama smiled. Then everyone picked up bread at the same time.

The next Sunday they came back. Ivy brought a small cup of juice. She set it down on the blanket. "First we say it," said Ivy. She held out her hands. Pop took one hand. Mama took the other.

"One, two, three," said Ivy. They said the greeting together. Then everyone ate. The grapes tasted sweet. A bird hopped close to the blanket. "Hello, bird," said Ivy. "You get bread after."

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
story:
Maverick went to Grandma's house. His toy pig was in his bag. The pig was cold from the car ride. Maverick wanted to warm it up.

He wrapped the pig in a small blanket. He patted the pig, pat, pat. Grandma watched from her chair. "Is piggy sleepy?" she asked. Maverick nodded. He rocked the pig in his arms. Then the pig made him feel like rocking too. When he rocked slow, the pig looked calm. When he rocked fast, the pig bounced and looked silly.

Maverick made a pretend bed from a soft towel. He tucked the pig in. "Night night, pig," he said in a polite little voice. He pushed the towel bed on the floor. The bed did a gentle swing from side to side. The pig slid off. Maverick laughed and picked the pig up. "More blanket," he said. He added another fold. This time the pig stayed snug.

Grandma hummed a quiet song. Maverick yawned. He lay down next to the pig on the rug. "Shh," he whispered. "Piggy is sleeping." Grandma covered them both with her warm, soft shawl. It smelled like sugar and lemons. Maverick closed his eyes.

activity: cooking or baking a meal for the family
knowledge_domain: cooking or baking a meal for the family
story:
Emma wants to make breakfast for her family. "Daddy, can I help cook?" she asks. Daddy says yes. They stand by the camp stove together. Daddy keeps Emma far from the hot pan. He holds the spoon. Emma cracks an egg into a bowl. Some shell falls in. Emma frowns. Her egg looks messy.

"Try again," says Daddy. Emma cracks another egg. This time the shell stays out. The egg looks smooth and yellow. Daddy pours it into the pan. The runny egg turns firm and white. Emma taps Daddy's arm. "Look! It got fat!" she says. Daddy smiles and flips the egg.

The egg goes on a plate with bread. Mommy takes a taste. "Yummy," she says. Baby brother claps. Near the tent, a green frog hops by. Emma waves at it. Then she sits close to Mommy and eats her egg all up.

activity: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
knowledge_domain: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
story:
Anna wanted to find her robot toy. She could not find it. Where did it go?

Anna looked with her eyes. She saw her blocks. She saw her bear. No robot there. Then Anna heard a little sound with her ears. Beep, beep! "Was that my robot?" she asked. "Yes, it was!"

The beeps came from under the blanket. Anna touched the blanket with her hands. It was soft and warm. She pulled the blanket back. There was her robot!

Anna was so happy. She was not sad anymore. Mom came in with warm cookies. Anna smelled them with her nose. Yum! She tasted a cookie with her tongue. Sweet!

Anna hugged her robot. "I found you," she said. Beep, beep, said the robot.

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
story:
Jake wanted to play house in his playroom. He set his gray robot on a little chair. He gave his teddy bear a spot on the rug. But teddy kept falling over. He would not sit up at all.

Jake tried to prop teddy against the wall. Teddy slid down again. Then Jake saw his soft blue blanket in the toy box. He had an idea. He spread the blanket on the rug. He laid teddy down on top of it. Teddy lay very still. He looked like he was sleeping.

Jake made his voice small and soft. "Shh," he said. "The baby is sleeping." He tucked the blanket around teddy. The blanket stayed put. Teddy did not fall over anymore.

Jake picked up his gray robot. "You are the big brother," he whispered. "We must be quiet." The robot sat by the chair. Jake patted teddy's head. He tried to make a lunch for everyone, too. He filled a toy pot with pretend soup.

Then teddy's eyes seemed to open. "Time to wake up," said Jake. He lifted teddy into a hug. "You slept so well. Now we can eat." The robot got a pretend bowl, too. Jake smiled and stirred the soup round and round. "More soup, anyone?"

activity: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
knowledge_domain: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
story: Austin ran to the big slide at the playground. Mommy came too. The big slide was tall. The small slide was short. Austin wanted to go fast, but the slide was hot from the sun. "Ouch," said Mommy. "We must wait. Hot things can hurt you." Austin touched the small slide. It was in the shade. The small slide felt cool. "This one is cold," said Austin. So Austin sat on the small slide. He went down slow. He went down slow, slow, slow. Then he tried again. He wiggled his feet. Now he went fast, fast, fast! He laughed loud. A big dog ran by. Then a small horse clip-clopped past the fence. The big dog ran fast. The small horse walked slow. "Big and small, fast and slow," said Austin. Mommy held his hand. They sat in the cool shade. Austin drank cold water from his cup. "Not alone," said Mommy. "I sit with you." Austin leaned on her arm and watched the small horse walk away.

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
story:
Nova got to Rosa's house early. Rosa's mom had not set out the toys yet.

"I want to play house," said Nova.

"Let's make a house," said Rosa.

They turned a big box over. Now it was a house with a door. Nova crawled in through the door. Rosa crawled in too.

But the baby dolls were sad on the shelf. Nova wanted to be the mom. She reached for the baby. The baby was too far up.

"Use the step stool," said Rosa.

Nova climbed the stool. She held the baby tight. It worked!

Nova wrapped the baby in a soft sock. She patted its back. The baby closed its eyes.

"Time for the bus," said Rosa. She pushed a chair to the box.

Nova held her baby and sat down. Vroom, vroom! The bus drove to the store.

Then the baby peeked out of the sock. It was wearing Rosa's tiny hat!

"How did that get there?" Nova asked.

Rosa just smiled and said, "Next stop, home!"

activity: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
knowledge_domain: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
story:
At daycare, Liam found a big cardboard box. "A boat!" he said. He was so excited. His hands jumped up and down.

Mia wanted the box too. She grabbed one side. Liam grabbed the other side. "Mine!" he shouted. His face got hot and red. He was angry now.

Then Mia began to cry. Big tears ran down her cheeks. Liam saw her sad face. He let go of the box. "You can go first," he said. Mia smiled a happy smile. The teacher patted Liam's head. "Kind hands," she said softly.

Suddenly the room got noisy. A loud truck went by the window. Liam felt scared. He held the teacher's hand. She gave him a gentle pat. "The truck is going away," she said. The sound got smaller and smaller. Liam climbed into the box. Mia pushed him slowly. "Boat ride!" she said. Liam laughed and laughed.

activity: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
knowledge_domain: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
story:
Emile ran to the art table. He wanted to paint a house for his toy dog. Miss Rosa gave him a big brush. "Paint something you like," she said.

Emile painted a square. It had four flat sides. He looked at it. A square made a good house! Then he painted a triangle on top. The triangle had three sides. It sat on the square like a roof. "A roof!" said Emile.

He painted little squares for windows. He painted a rectangle door. The rectangle was long, not tall like the door. Wait. His door looked wrong. Miss Rosa turned the rectangle the other way. Now it was tall. Now it looked like a door.

Emile painted a yellow circle at the top. The circle had no sides at all. It glowed like a sun over the house. He held up his painting. "My dog has a home!" he said. Miss Rosa clapped. Emile put his toy dog on the table, right under the circle sun.

activity: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
knowledge_domain: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
story:
Eva went to the playground with Grandma. "Stay where I can see you," said Grandma. Eva nodded. She wanted to find the best spot to play.

Eva counted as she walked. One bench, two swings, three slides. The metal slide sat in the sun. Eva put her hand near it. The slide was hot, very hot. Grandma held Eva's hand. They walked to the shady slide instead. Eva touched it. This one was cool. Down she went, whee!

Then Eva saw something shiny in the grass. It was a bit of broken glass. She reached out. "Stop," said Grandma. "We don't touch sharp things." Grandma picked it up with a glove and put it far away. Eva watched the whole time.

"I found a cool slide," said Eva. "And a hot one too." Grandma smiled. Eva counted again. One bench, two swings, two slides. Then she ran back to the swings, right where Grandma could see her.

activity: to name the primary colours and mix two of them to make a new colour
knowledge_domain: to name the primary colours and mix two of them to make a new colour
story:
Zoe wanted to paint a big orange leaf for the fall wall. But the paint pots had no orange. There was red, yellow, and blue. Zoe looked and looked. No orange anywhere.

Zoe held up the red pot. "This is red," she said. She held up the yellow. "This is yellow." She pointed at the last one. "And that is blue." Her teacher smiled and gave her a big white tray.

Zoe put a dot of red on the tray. Then she put a dot of yellow next to it. She mixed them with her brush, round and round. The dots turned orange, bright as a pumpkin. Zoe gasped. Two paints had made a new paint!

She painted her leaf with the orange. It looked like fire from a dragon, she thought. Her polite friend Ben came over and asked, "Can I try?" Zoe put more red and more yellow on the tray. She gave him the brush.

"You go round and round," she said. "Watch what happens."

activity: to throw a beanbag into a hoop and catch a large ball with both hands
knowledge_domain: to throw a beanbag into a hoop and catch a large ball with both hands
story:
Sebastian stood in the backyard. He held a red beanbag in his hand. A hoop lay on the grass like a big circle. He wanted the beanbag to land inside it.

Sebastian threw the beanbag. It flew past the hoop. It landed in the flowers. He ran and picked it up. He stood close to the hoop this time. He tossed the beanbag down. It went right into the circle. Sebastian clapped his hands.

Then Dad brought a big yellow ball. "Catch it with both hands," said Dad. Dad rolled the ball slowly. Sebastian held out one hand. The ball bounced off and rolled away. He ran after it across the busy yard.

Sebastian tried again. This time he covered the ball with two hands. Both hands held it tight. The ball stopped. It did not roll away. "I caught it!" said Sebastian. Dad smiled and rolled the ball again. Sebastian held out both arms and waited.

activity: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
knowledge_domain: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
story:
It was a hot summer day. Ivy wanted to go down the big slide. But the slide was busy. Lots of kids were waiting.

Ivy stood in line. A big kid began to count. "One, two, three," he said. Each time he said a number, one kid went down. Whoosh! The line got shorter.

Ivy listened. "Four, five, six." Three more kids slid down, fast. The sun was warm on her head. Her water bottle almost fell. She was careful and held it tight so it would not spill.

The big kid said, "Seven, eight, nine." Now only one kid was left. Then it was Ivy's turn. "Ten!" said the big kid. Ivy climbed up and sat down. She held on tight.

Whoosh! Down she went, fast and smiling.

"My turn to count," said Ivy. She stood by the slide and began, "One, two..."

activity: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
knowledge_domain: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
story:
Olivier held a tiny seed in his hand. It was small and brown. "Will this really make a carrot?" he asked. Grandma smiled. "Put it in the dirt and see."

Olivier made a little hole. He dropped the seed in. He patted the dirt on top, soft and flat. "Sleep well, little seed," he said.

Every day Olivier came to the garden. He looked and looked. One morning, a green leaf popped up! "Grandma, come quick!" he called. The leaf was small and wet from the rain. More rain fell. The leaf grew taller. Then more leaves came.

But one plant was droopy. It looked sad and flat. "Why is it bendy?" Olivier wondered. Grandma let him fill a small watering can. Olivier poured water on the dirt. The next day, the plant stood up tall.

Olivier picked a pink flower growing near the carrots. He put it by the plant as a gift. Then Grandma handed him a cookie for a snack. He munched and watched his garden. "Hello, little leaf," he said. "Grow big like me."

activity: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story: Eliana was at Grandma's house. She found a purple book on the big chair. "That is my library book," said Grandma. Eliana wanted to keep it forever. It had a bear who could crawl into tiny caves. Grandma opened the book. She began at the front. The bear crawled on page one. Then page two. Then page three. "The bear goes this way," said Eliana, pointing. She turned the pages herself. She touched the little marks under the bear. "What are these?" she asked. "Those are words," said Grandma. "They say what the bear does." Eliana looked closely. The words made the bear crawl. But then Grandma said, "We must take the book back on Friday. Then other kids can read it." Eliana hugged the book tight. She read it all week. On Friday, Grandma helped her put it in a bag. At the library, Eliana set the book on the desk. The librarian smiled. She handed Eliana a shiny stamp card. "Want to pick a new one?" she asked. Eliana ran to the shelves. "I want a book with a map in it," she said.

activity: getting a vaccination shot at the doctor's office
knowledge_domain: getting a vaccination shot at the doctor's office
story:
Isaac sat in the waiting room with his father. He hugged his favorite teddy bear. Today Isaac would get a shot. He did not want a shot.

"Shots feel like a quick pinch," said his father. "You can squeeze teddy tight."

Isaac squeezed teddy tight. The nurse came in. She wiped Isaac's arm with a cold, wet wipe. Then came the quick pinch.

"Ow," said Isaac. He squeezed teddy even tighter. Then the pinch stopped. The nurse put a round bandage on his arm.

"Done," said the nurse. "You were so brave."

Isaac looked at the bandage. His father held up a sticker. It had a red fire truck on it.

Isaac took the sticker. He pressed it right onto teddy's paw. "Teddy got a bandage too," he said.

His father laughed. "Let's go home, big boy."

activity: spending a surprise snow day at home
knowledge_domain: spending a surprise snow day at home
story:
Elena woke up and saw white outside. Snow! Lots and lots of snow. No school today!

She pulled on her boots. She pulled on her red coat. "Mom, can I build a snowman?" Mom said yes. Out they went into the cold.

The snow was deep and soft. Elena patted a big ball. She patted and patted. But the snow would not stick. It kept falling off. The snowman had no head. Elena felt grumpy. She stomped her boot. "Why won't it stay on?"

Then she saw Dad shoveling. The shovel made a loud sound, like a hammer hitting the ground. The snow on his pile looked shiny and packed down tight.

Elena picked up some snow. She squeezed it in her mittens. It clumped into a hard ball. She squeezed some more, and it stuck!

She packed the head tight. Up it went, and it stayed! "My snowman has a head! My snowman has a head!" Elena put a carrot nose on him. "Now let's make him a friend," she said, grabbing more snow.

activity: starting the first day of school
knowledge_domain: starting the first day of school
story:
Matteo woke up in his dark room. Today was his first day of school. He wanted to pack his own backpack. He put in his crayons. He put in his bear. But the zipper would not close.

"Let me try again," said Matteo. He pulled one side. It did not move. He pulled the other side. It did not move. He sat down and looked at the zipper. The two sides were apart. He pushed the two sides together. He heard a little click.

Now he pulled the zipper. It moved all the way up. The backpack was closed! His crayons were inside. His bear was inside too. Matteo put the backpack on his back. His shoes sat by the door. He pushed his foot into each one.

Mama smiled. "Ready for school?" she asked. Matteo ran to the door. "Yes! I did it all by myself!"

activity: searching for a lost favorite toy
knowledge_domain: searching for a lost favorite toy
story:
Jasper looked in the sandbox. "One, no truck," he said. His special blue truck was lost.

Miss Rosa came to help. "Let's look together," she said. They looked by the slide. "Two, no truck." They looked under the bench. "Three, no truck."

The wind blew. A big leaf flew past Jasper's foot. The wind pushed the leaf along the ground. Jasper watched it slide under the little gate. "The wind pushes things," he thought.

Jasper ran to the gate. He peeked under it. There was his truck! The wind had pushed it there too. Miss Rosa opened the gate. "My truck!" said Jasper. He hugged it tight.

"Let's fix a safe pocket for it," said Miss Rosa. She put the truck in Jasper's coat pocket. Jasper patted the pocket. "One truck, all safe," he said.

activity: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
knowledge_domain: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
story:
William wanted the big red truck. His sister Mia had it first. William grabbed the truck. Mia cried loud. The truck fell on the rug.

Mummy knelt down. "We take turns," she said. "William, you can have the truck after Mia." William sat on the rug. He waited. He stacked two soft blocks. He stacked three. Then four.

Mia pushed the truck fast across the floor. It bumped the blocks. The blocks fell down. Mia laughed. Then she held out the truck. "Your turn," she said.

William took the truck. He pushed it fast, too. Mia waited, just like William had done. Then it was her turn again.

Soon it was dinner time. William put the truck on the shelf. He shut the toy box lid. "Truck sleeps now," he said. Mia patted the box. "Night night, truck."

activity: to name the five senses and say which body part is used for each
knowledge_domain: to name the five senses and say which body part is used for each
story:
Florence wanted to play a guessing game. Grandma said, "I will guess things. You tell me how you know."

Grandma hid a pink flower behind her back. "Sniff, sniff," she said. Florence shouted, "Nose! You smell it with your nose!"

Then Grandma rang a little bell. Florence covered her ears. "Ears! We hear with ears!"

Grandma held up the flower. "Now look." Florence giggled. "Eyes! Eyes see the pink!"

Grandma let Florence touch the grass. "Toes feel tickly grass," Florence said. "Skin feels it!"

One thing was left. Grandma pointed to her tongue. "Taste! But do not lick the flower," Grandma said. She got a tiny cookie from her pocket. Florence took a small bite. "Mmm! Tongue tastes cookies!"

Grandma counted on her fingers. "Nose, ears, eyes, skin, tongue. Five!" Florence counted too. "Nose, ears, eyes, skin, tongue!"

Then Florence ran to the swing and shouted, "My skin feels the wind!"

activity: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
knowledge_domain: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
story:
Connor ran to the big slide at the playground. But a girl was already at the top. She sat down and slid. A boy climbed up next. Then it was Connor's turn. He slid down fast. Whee!

Connor wanted to go again. He ran to the ladder. But two kids were already waiting in line. Connor stopped and stood behind them. "Why do we wait?" he asked. "So everyone gets a turn," said the girl in front. One kid went down. Then the next kid went down. Then it was Connor again.

Near the sandbox, a boy was digging. His shovel was hard at work. Connor wanted a shovel too. There was only one. "Can I have a turn?" Connor asked. "Yes, when I am done," said the boy. He dug three more scoops. Then he held out the shovel. "Here you come," he said, and smiled. Connor dug a big hole.

A teacher clapped her hands. "Snack time," she called. "Wash hands first." Connor got in line at the water fountain. He waited. He washed. Then he sat on the bench with his present from home, a little bag of crackers. The girl sat next to him with no snack. Connor held out the bag. "Want some?" he asked. She took one cracker and said, "Thank you."

activity: playing on a sports team for the season
knowledge_domain: playing on a sports team for the season
story:
Sophie put on her red team shirt. It was her first day of soccer at the park. Grandpa held her hand on the gray sidewalk. "Where is my team?" Sophie asked. Grandpa pointed to the kids by the goal.

Coach Nina gave Sophie a ball. Sophie tapped it with her toe. The ball rolled a tiny bit and stopped. She tapped it again, soft. It rolled a tiny bit again. Then Sophie pulled her leg back and kicked the ball hard. The ball rolled far, far away, all the way past the cones.

Sophie ran after it. "Grandpa, did you see?" she called. "I kicked it and it went far!" Grandpa smiled and waved. A boy named Tom began to cry because the ball bumped his foot. Coach Nina knelt down and gave him a soft pat.

"Try again," Coach Nina said to Sophie. Sophie looked at the goal. She kicked the ball hard with her whole foot. The ball rolled and rolled, right into the net. "Goal!" the team shouted. Sophie jumped up and down. Then she lined up the ball one more time.

activity: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
knowledge_domain: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
story:
Olivier sat in the waiting room with his mama. They were late, so they hurried in. Olivier wanted the turtle sticker at the front desk. But first he had to wait for his turn.

Then he heard a plane. It went over the roof. Rrrrrrumble. Olivier put his hands over his ears. The sound got small. He took his hands off. The rumble came back, big and loud. He did it again. Hands on, hands off. "Mama, my ears make it quiet!"

A nurse called his name. In the small room, the doctor came in. She looked in Olivier's eyes. "Your eyes see me," she said. Olivier saw her shiny blue pen light blink.

She looked in his nose. "Sniff this little tube," she said. Olivier sniffed with his nose. It smelled like soap. Then the doctor put a tiny stick near his mouth. "Say ahh." Olivier tasted something sweet, like a berry.

The doctor pressed softly on his tummy. "Your skin can feel my hands," she said. Olivier felt the warm press. He touched the paper on the bed. It was crinkly and smooth.

At the front desk, Olivier picked his turtle sticker. He pressed it with his finger. It stuck tight to his shirt. Outside, another plane went by. Olivier kept his ears open all the way home.

activity: going on a family trip away from home
knowledge_domain: going on a family trip away from home
story:
Zayn stood on the ferry with his dad. The big boat was taking them on a trip. Zayn held his bag of crackers. He was hungry, so he ate one. He dropped some crumbs on the deck. Then a big white bird flew down. The bird picked up the crumbs with its beak. Zayn was surprised. One cracker had made a bird come!

Zayn wanted the bird to come again. He broke off a little piece of cracker. He dropped it on the deck. The bird swooped down and took it. Then more birds came. They all wanted crumbs. Dad laughed softly. "Slow down," he said. "Save some for later." Zayn held his bag tight. He dropped just one more piece, and one more bird came.

Then the wind blew. It blew Zayn's little paper hat right off his head. The hat rolled along the deck. A kind lady picked it up. She smiled and gave it back. "Thank you," said Zayn.

Later, they went inside the ferry. It was warm there. Dad stirred sugar into his tea. Dad let Zayn watch from his safe seat. Zayn had a seed and nut mix in his pocket. He munched it slowly. The ferry smelled a bit stinky, like the sea. Zayn looked out the big window. He saw the waves go up and down. The boat went up and down too. Zayn waved at the water. "Bye bye, waves," he said. "See you on our trip home."

activity: to throw a beanbag into a hoop and catch a large ball with both hands
knowledge_domain: to throw a beanbag into a hoop and catch a large ball with both hands
story:
Hannah stood in the big school gym. She held a small red beanbag. She wanted to throw it into the hoop on the floor. She threw it. It hit the edge and fell out. "Why did it fall?" she asked. Teacher Mia smiled. "Try standing closer," she said.

Hannah took two steps closer. She threw the beanbag again. It went up, then down. Plunk! It landed inside the hoop. "It went in!" said Hannah. She jumped up and down.

Next, Mia rolled her a big ball. It was too big for one hand. It bumped Hannah's tummy and fell. "Why can't I hold it?" asked Hannah. She looked at her hands. She put out both hands this time. Mia rolled the ball again. Hannah caught it with both arms. The ball stayed. "I did it!" she said. Mia clapped, and the ball flew up in the air between them.

activity: making an art or craft project
knowledge_domain: making an art or craft project
story:
Asher went to the library. There was a craft table with paper and crayons. Asher wanted to make a rainbow picture.

The librarian gave him a black crayon. "Color your whole paper black," she said. Asher pressed hard. He covered all the colors. Now his paper was all black. Where did the rainbow go?

Then the librarian gave him a little stick. "Try a scratch," she said. Asher dragged the stick across the paper. A red line appeared! He scratched again. A green line popped out! The rainbow was hiding under the black. Asher scratched and scratched. A sun came out. A fish came out. A big rainbow came out too.

A girl sat down next to Asher. She looked sad. "My paper is all black," she said. Asher handed her his stick. "Scratch it," he said. She scratched a yellow star. She smiled big. "Let's make more," Asher said, and handed her another stick.

activity: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
knowledge_domain: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
story:
William sat in his car seat. He looked out the window. "I want my snack," he said.

Mom reached into the bag. "Let's find it," she said. "We have a banana. We have crackers. We have cheese." William pointed. "The banana!" The banana was a food. He loved it best.

William peeled it a little. The peel opened like a big yellow jacket. He held on tight. The car went bump. The banana slipped. It began to fall! "Oh no!" said William. Mom caught it in her hand. "Safe," she said. William took a big bite. The banana made him happy.

After the snack, they played a game. "Tell me what you see," said Mom. William saw a cow. The cow was an animal. "Moo!" said William. He saw a dog in a truck. The dog was an animal too. "Woof!" said William. Mom laughed.

Then William dropped his toy truck. It slid under the seat. "My truck!" he said. Mom stopped at a red light. She reached down. She found the truck and a soft ball. The truck and the ball were toys. William hugged them. "My truck, my ball," he said. "One animal, one food, one toy," said Mom. The light turned green. "Moo!" said William, and off they went.

activity: searching for a lost favorite toy
knowledge_domain: searching for a lost favorite toy
story:
Evelyn went to the park with her blue bunny. She carried bunny in her arms all morning. Then it was time for a snack. Evelyn put bunny down on the grass.

After the snack, bunny was gone. "Where did bunny go?" she asked. "Let's look," said Dad.

They looked by the swing. No bunny. They looked under the bench. No bunny. "One swing, one bench," said Evelyn. "No bunny."

Then the wind blew. The wind made the big leaves move. Evelyn saw the leaves flip up and down. Something blue was under the leaves! She ran over and pushed the leaves apart. There was bunny, smiling up at her.

"The wind showed me!" said Evelyn. She hugged bunny tight. Then she carried bunny to the sandbox. "You sit here," she said. "Right next to me."

Dad sat down too. Evelyn made a little cake from sand. She put a small rock on top. "One cake, one rock, one bunny," she said. "All here."

activity: to share a toy with a classmate and wait for a turn without grabbing
knowledge_domain: to share a toy with a classmate and wait for a turn without grabbing
story:
Noah went to soccer practice. Coach Maya had one big red ball. All the kids wanted it.

Noah grabbed the ball first. He held it tight. Ben reached for it too. Then Ben got mad. His face turned red. He sat down on the grass and would not look at Noah.

Coach Maya knelt beside them. "We can write our turn list on my clipboard," she said. She wrote NOAH first. Then she wrote BEN under it. Noah looked at the list. His name was on top. He kicked the ball to Ben, and Ben kicked it back. When Noah waited, he got his turn again.

Then Noah sat down next to Ben. "Your turn now," Noah said. He pointed at the list. Ben smiled and stood up fast. He ran with the ball all the way to the net. Noah clapped his hands.

After practice, Coach Maya gave out juice. Ben drew a picture in the dirt with a stick. It was a big blue ocean with a soccer ball floating on a wave. "That is for you," Ben said. Noah sat close to his coach and held his juice. "Same time tomorrow," said Coach Maya. Noah waved to Ben all the way to the car.
